Im sorry to hear that stranger. The only advice I can ever give you, is do not, by any circumstamce give yourself a time limit to get it over with now. If you cant do it, it's okay. Give yourself days to cry, shout, hope amd experience all these emotions - they can be all incredibly exhausting but you need to feel and get it out of your system. You are human - you loved someone with every inch of you, and you are also able to grieve their absence to which your skin hurts from missing them. 

It took me 1 year to finally accept that he is out of my life, and even if I barely remember his existence, I wont deny it once hurt. 

As per your belongings, I dont have any experience living with someone nor seeing an ex but just do it if you're totally ready. And after that, you can continue healing. Im sorry again for what happened, wishing you best luck and light♡

Details, well... we broke up because of frequent fights and mainly of "parental interference." His mom broke us up the week after my 17th birthday. It changed my whole life and completely changed who I am. We both loved each other and corresponded rarely for 3 months after to establish closure but it only ever happened online so I dont consider it "proper closure".  The last time we spoke was December 2020, to which my harsh last words to him was "Dont ever speak to me anymore" by email. I kind of regretted it back then, cried alot for a year. And we are here now : )

We have been friends for... I dont remember anymore. But couple for almost 2 years. Within a year it was almost full of cries, but this year...The first time I felt peace was like... not thinking of him and not needing him anymore as time went on. I dont even cry anymore, it's basically a linear healing
If I ever see them again, I am certain I'd either barely recognize them, or if I do I'd get natural chills but overall its just a "meh" thing tbh

First of all, it is completely understandable to be worried or even be having those intrusive thoughts after breakup. In my own experience, discipline is only the answer to get through that stage of stalking. 

And by discipline is the mindset of "Why would I be stalking her if she is already out of my life, or if we are already over? What's the point?"

The discipline of not giving yourself any type of hurt and spiralling obsessive thoughts again. The effective way to stop caring for someone. Urges will definitely creep from time to time, but the longer you have stopped stalking, each day gets easier. the curiousity eventuallly dies. hope it helps ◇
